title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 23 | Week 7 vs. Denver Broncos
headline: Jeremiyah Love is out Sunday vs. Denver, so Tyler Allgeier (third downs, short yardage) and Bam Knight (early downs) lead the backfield; Budda Baker, Darius Robinson and Max Melton are being monitored up to game time.
summary: LaFleur opened with the injury report: Love is out Sunday, along with two others who were named only in garbled captions. Jon Gaines also picked up an ankle injury in practice and is out, so Hayden Conner steps in. A quarterback named 'Carson' left practice early with back spasms, which LaFleur called minor and not long term. Baker, Robinson and Melton are all being monitored, with Robinson's status to be watched up to game time. LaFleur said he is not considering putting Love on IR and doesn't expect IR for Wills, though he conceded anything can happen. On the backfield, he described Allgeier as the third-down and short-yardage back and Knight as the early-down back, and said he doesn't want either carrying a 65-70 play workload. He praised Denver's defense for its scheme conviction, its players and its motor, and expects a mix of coverages. He expects Bo Nix and Denver's offense at their best, and said the red zone gets emphasis today without any panic. He wants a good home performance on the day Larry Fitzgerald is honored at halftime.

Minter expects to settle the injury designation within hours, and a questionable tag is the likely outcome. He said the process could run up to game time and the next 48 hours will be telling. He described Jackson as super competitive and eager to play. On the secondary, he cited depth, with Chidobe Awuzie potentially getting more snaps alongside other safeties, and Kyle Hamilton able to move around. On the edge, he said Zion Young and Ethan Burke are no longer rookies in feel and should see more snaps with Robinson out.

title: Dave Canales: 'We're excited for a championship opportunity'
headline: Monroe Freeling is back from his knee injury and looked great, though Dave Canales won't say whether he'll start over Rasheed Walker. Trevor Etienne may be active as a fourth RB mainly for special teams, and Panthers running-game efficiency is a work in progress against Tampa's top run defense.
summary: Canales is excited about a 'championship opportunity' at home against the division-rival Buccaneers. He praised Monroe Freeling's week of work coming back from a knee injury but declined to say whether Freeling will take over from the current offensive line setup, only that he 'could' help. The Panthers rank last in first-half rushing and second-best in the second half, and Canales said the fix is more efficient early runs (2nd-and-6 or less) rather than 'establishing the run.' He credited Philadelphia's and Tampa's defenses, and Todd Bowles' run-stopping emphasis, for the early struggles. He expects Baker Mayfield to start for Tampa in a custom glove after a hand or finger injury, comparing it to Russell Wilson's finger injury in Seattle. Trevor Etienne is making an impact on special teams (returns, a blocked punt, coverage), so activating four running backs is a possibility. Thomas Incoom's absence opens special-teams and leadership roles for players like Nick Hampton. Injured players are progressing: one is 'crushing his rehab' and Michael Jackson is picking up speed. Change of direction is the limiting factor, and they must clear four games on IR first.

title: Ben Johnson on Bears' Thursday night victory over Patriots | Press Conference
headline: Cole Kmet left the 30-24 win over New England with a knee injury that Johnson said 'didn't look very good'. Luther Burden III, Colston Loveland and Rome Odunze all produced, and Caleb Williams topped 300 yards.
summary: Johnson was proud of the team after a physical Thursday night win on a short week. He said the game had many ups and downs and took all 60 minutes to win. He opened with two injuries, one to a toe (the player's name was cut off) and one to Cole Kmet's knee, and said more information would come the next day. Asked about Kmet, he said he didn't think the injury looked good. He praised the pass catchers, saying Luther Burden III gave an early spark, Colston Loveland took over in the middle of the game, and Rome Odunze made big plays late. He called Caleb Williams' night good, noting several explosive plays, completions to the second level, and extended drives on third down while the run game was slow to get going. He said Williams has now found open receivers two weeks in a row. He also credited special teams, including the onside kick recovery, strong kickoff coverage, a kick return from Zavion Thomas, and a 58-yard field goal late. Johnson said the decision to attempt it was close, but the kicker's pregame numbers and his own insistence on redemption after an earlier miss made them comfortable. He added that he is more comfortable calling plays after a full week of practice, which this short week didn't allow.

title: Ben Johnson reviews Thursday's victory, gives update on Cole Kmet | Press Conference
headline: Cole Kmet is done for the season with a serious knee injury and headed to IR; Sam Roush's snaps should rise, while Luther Burden and Colston Loveland continue to emerge in a spread-the-ball passing attack.
summary: Johnson opened by praising the team for winning a short-week game against the Patriots, then confirmed that Cole Kmet has a serious knee injury, is out for the season, and goes on IR today. He said Kmet's absence won't change the playbook because all the tight ends are trained to do every job, and he named Sam Roush as the first beneficiary, with a high likelihood that his rep count rises. He floated more jumbo packages if Ozzy Trapilo keeps trending up, and mentioned Hayden Large (on IR) and practice-squad tight ends as depth options. Johnson was very positive on Luther Burden, who sparked the first half and is elite with the ball in his hands. He wants to get Burden deep more and said Burden's intermediate route detail is encouraging. Colston Loveland's target share has been rising despite a couple of uncharacteristic drops, and Rome Odunze closed the game strong. Caleb Williams was praised for speeding up his progressions and taking fewer negative plays, though he was still sacked three times. Johnson took blame for not telling Williams that yardage mattered more than the clock before the 58-yard field goal. He also noted the offense has too many pre-snap and holding penalties. Jonah Jackson played every snap after a short turnaround, and Theo Benedet is doing a solid job at left tackle. The defense has improved against the run, but it still needs more takeaways.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference : October 23rd, 2026
headline: Judkins and Dylan Sampson are both expected back together for the first time since Week 1, with Sampson pegged as a screen-game weapon. Mason Graham is back, and Grant Delpit's concussion clearance is due Saturday.
summary: Monken said Mason Graham is back and ready after an injury that turned out less serious than feared. Grant Delpit is still in the protocol and has one final hurdle to clear, which Monken expects tomorrow. A Denzel with a finger injury showed up on the injury report, and Monken expects him to play. It's unclear whether that is Ward or Boston. Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson are expected back together for the first time since the opener, which Monken called a boost for a running game and an offense that still needs to be better. Sampson has taken another step forward, and Monken called him explosive and a weapon, especially on screens. He credited Jaleel McLaughlin and the backs for last week's performance. Monken did not deflect blame for the slow offensive starts: the scheme, coaching and execution all need to improve, and the offense is still under construction. He praised Maliek Collins as a disruptive, leading veteran and Carson Schwesinger as a smart linebacker who is playing through an ankle injury. The team is 4-2 and faces a Titans defense whose structure is similar to Cleveland's.

title: HC Sean Payton on the importance of stacking wins: ‘We have to be ascending [and] improving’
headline: Jonah Coleman is likely back from his four-week injury absence but on a pitch count, and Payton gave no starting-lineup info for Arizona.
summary: Payton spoke on Friday before Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals and kept it week-by-week, saying the team must be "ascending, improving" and can't yo-yo. He said players returning from reserve/injured, such as Jonah Coleman (out four weeks) and a player captioned as Jonathan Cooper, will be tracked closely on a pitch count, especially after a month or more away. He declined to announce starters. He downplayed having Bo Nix run more, saying it isn't a top-ten priority. He explained his fullback preference: he likes a true F, but Nate Adkins could fill those roles if needed. Adam Trautman's snaps depend on whether the game plan targets the opponent's base or sub defense. He praised Zach Allen's tape and Ja'Quan McMillian's play at nickel. He said running back usage weighs third-down and two-minute pass-catching against pass protection, and he liked an unnamed back's progress, probably RJ Harvey. He also stressed depth, especially at corner, and said Kansas City wasn't on his mind yet.

title: Campbell on preparing for Green Bay
headline: Brian Branch is cleared to play (with some caution) vs. Green Bay, Cade Mays is moving into the starting C spot over Juice Scruggs, and Campbell shut down the Sam LaPorta comments as a non-issue.
summary: Campbell said Cade Mays and Brian Branch are both doing well and the team is finishing a good week of preparation, with red zone work on the third practice day. He has a pretty good idea of Branch's role and said they will let him go but be smart about it, and that Branch is ready to play. He explained that the move to Mays at center is about finding the best five linemen: Mays is a different type of player than Juice Scruggs, and Scruggs will still be involved going forward. He said he does not worry about Sam LaPorta's Pardon My Take comments, called LaPorta a stud and an unselfish teammate who will help win games, and refused to keep revisiting it. On the player who has been in the contract or business story, Campbell said the player has been locked in all week and is ready to be used, though he never names him in this transcript. He praised Jordan Love and the Green Bay offense for their deep passing and said Love is playing as well as anyone at quarterback. He described Green Bay's defense as playing as one unit, aggressive and physical, with seven takeaways in two weeks, and said this is a big divisional challenge. He wants Detroit to play cleaner than they did against Arizona, and he said he is excited about DeAndre Carter as a returner, having lost Tom Kennedy.

title: Sean McVay speaks on competing with no regrets, scouting the Raiders, Myles Garrett's progress & more
headline: Puka Nacua (calf) is questionable and a pregame decision after missing practice, while Trent McDuffie is questionable and Nate Landman is out; Myles Garrett could begin practicing next week.

Myles Garrett has been rehabbing but is present in meetings and well respected by teammates. title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 10/22: "We did some good things, just didn't do enough"
headline: Patriots lost a close Week 7 game to the Bears on Thursday night; Drake Maye earned praise despite a late turnover, and TreVeyon Henderson's snaps dipped while Corey Kiner got a few carries.
summary: Vrabel said the loss came down to thin margins: poor tackling, a turnover, and failing to get enough red-zone stops or convert their one red-zone chance. He said the Patriots fought and gave themselves a chance, but didn't do enough. He praised Drake Maye for competing, scrambling and finding good places to go with the ball, and he is glad Maye is his quarterback. Maye would like to have one throw back, and Vrabel said he will learn from it. The offense started with several three-and-outs, then improved once it played more connected and protected well against heavy Bears pressure, which produced chunk plays in the second half. The run game wasn't good enough, but the passing game moved the ball. Henderson was off the field for a stretch because of packages and personnel groupings, and Kiner got a couple of carries. Vrabel was noncommittal on the fill-in offensive linemen Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor, saying only that they competed and that the penalties hurt more than the protection. He declined to say injuries at cornerback were a factor and said the injured players will be slotted in once they are available.
